raw_text:
Thanks — I’ll build a 12-week, resistance-centred program focused on improving body composition and insulin sensitivity while minimizing risk of under-fuelling and HPA-axis stress. I’ll avoid excessive cardio and high-volume depletion, include progressive resistance training, structured recovery, and nutrition guidance aimed at steady, sustainable changes (no crash diets). Because her cycle is irregular and sometimes anovulatory, I’ll avoid strict cycle-phase-dependent programming and instead use a steady, conservative progression with auto-regulation cues (energy, sleep, mood) to reduce risk of overtraining.

Summary targets
- Primary goals: improve insulin sensitivity, reduce fat mass while preserving/adding lean mass, support metabolic health.
- Training frequency: 3 full-body resistance sessions/week + 1 optional low-impact metabolic/conditioning session every 7–10 days (or replaced by active recovery). Total weekly training time ≈ 3–4 sessions, 45–75 min each.
- Progression: linear-to-undulating over 12 weeks with controlled increases in load/intensity and planned deload in week 7 and week 12 taper/review.
- Cardio: low-to-moderate volume, low-impact intervals or brisk walking 1–2×/week optional (20–30 min) to limit HPA stress.
- Nutrition: avoid aggressive deficits. Aim for modest caloric deficit (~ -200 to -350 kcal/day) if weight loss desired, prioritize protein (1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight/day), distribute carbohydrate around training to support performance and insulin sensitivity, sufficient fats for hormones, and ensure adequate micronutrients and fiber. Encourage regular meals/snacks to avoid long fasts that could stress HPA axis.
- Recovery: emphasize sleep (7–9 h), 1–2 full rest days/week, mobility and breathing work, monitor RPE, mood, resting HR / HRV if available.

Client specifics for programming
- Age 31, female, recreational lifter — can handle compound lifts and moderate intensity.
- PCOS (Rotterdam), irregular cycles — emphasis on resistance training and insulin-sensitizing interventions; avoid high-volume cardio or crash dieting.
- HbA1c 5.8 (prediabetes range) — focus on improving glycemic control through resistance training, protein, and meal timing.
- BMI 28 — aim for body composition shift not rapid weight loss.
- Endocrinologist clearance for full exercise.

Program overview (12 weeks): three 4-week blocks
- Block A (Weeks 1–4): Foundation — technique, movement variety, moderate volume, strength base, metabolic conditioning twice monthly. Emphasize protein, slightly reduced calories if desired, avoid aggressive deficits.
- Block B (Weeks 5–8): Build — increase intensity and load, introduce moderate hypertrophy phases, slightly higher RPE, include one metabolic session every week or every 7–10 days. Deload in Week 7 (reduced volume).
- Block C (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate & peak — maintain strength, slightly higher loading on key lifts, lower volume in final week for recovery/assessment, focus on consistency and adherence. Week 12 is a testing/review and planned reduced load.

Weekly structure (standard)
- Day 1 (Mon): Full-body strength priority A (heavy-ish)
- Day 2 (Wed): Full-body strength/upper emphasis or push/pull balance (moderate)
- Day 3 (Fri): Full-body strength priority B / lower emphasis + posterior chain
- Optional Day 4 (every 7–10 days): Low-impact conditioning (bike/row/brisk walk) 20–30 min, or mobility + breathing session
- Rest days: at least 1–2 full rest days per week, active recovery encouraged.

Progression and autoregulation cues
- Rate of perceived exertion (RPE) or Reps in Reserve (RIR) approach: start sets at ~2 RIR (i.e., leave 2 reps in tank) in early weeks and gradually push to 0–1 RIR on last sets of heavy work in block B/C.
- If energy/mood/sleep poor or resting HR elevated >5–8 bpm over baseline, reduce session intensity or replace with mobility/breathing.
- Avoid consecutive high-intensity days; monitor volume.

Sets, reps and intensity overview
- Compound lifts (squats, deadlifts, bench, rows, overhead press) in 3–5 sets of 4–8 reps at moderate-to-heavy loads.
- Hypertrophy accessory work 3–4 sets of 8–15 reps.
- Tempo controlled (2–1–2 for many accessory lifts), avoid excessive time-under-tension in the same session that could increase systemic stress.
- Rest 90–180s for heavy compound sets, 60–90s for accessory/hypertrophy.

Detailed week-by-week plan
Notes before starting each week: do a 5–10 min dynamic warm-up before sessions (foam rolling, hip/shoulder mobility, glute activation, light cardio), and a 5–10 min cool-down (mobility, breathing, light stretching). Prioritize progressive overload via load, reps, or minor increases in sets every 1–2 weeks as tolerated.

Block A — Foundation (Weeks 1–4)
Goal: movement quality, build base strength, establish routine and nutrition habits.

Week 1 (2026-06-01 start)
Session A (Day 1)
- Squat (back or goblet) 4×6 @ ~70% 1RM (RPE ~7, leave ~2 RIR)
- Romanian deadlift 3×8 (focus hip hinge)
- Incline dumbbell press 3×8–10
- Seated cable row 3×8–10
- Plank 3×30–45s
- Farmer carry 2×40m

Session B (Day 3)
- Deadlift variation (trap bar or conventional) 4×5 @ 70% 1RM
- Overhead press 3×6–8
- Split squat or Bulgarian 3×8 each leg
- Lat pulldown or pull-up progression 3×8–10
- Pallof press 3×12 each side

Session C (Day 5)
- Hip thrust 4×8–10
- Single-arm dumbbell row 3×10 each
- Dumbbell bench press 3×10
- Hamstring curl (machine) 3×12
- Glute bridge + banded walk circuit 3 rounds

Optional conditioning 1 (any 7–10 days)
- Bike or row steady 20 min, easy-moderate (RPE 4–5), or brisk walk 30 min

Nutrition & recovery for Week 1
- Protein target 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day (at bodyweight; e.g., if 70 kg → 112–140 g/day).
- Slight caloric deficit if weight loss desired: ~200–300 kcal/day below maintenance; ensure at least 1,600–1,800 kcal/day depending on baseline (no crash).
- Carbs focused around training (pre- and post-workout snack/meal).
- Sleep 7–9 hours, add evening breathing/relaxation 5–10 min.

Week 2
- Keep same session structure. Increase one variable: add 1–2 reps per set on main lifts or add 2.5–5% load if technique solid.
- Maintain RPE target (last set RPE ~7–8).
- Continue optional conditioning once.

Week 3
- Small progressive increase: for heavy compounds, 4×5 or 5×5 on one lift this week for stimulus; keep accessory volumes similar.
- Add tempo focus on eccentrics for 1–2 accessory lifts (3–1–1).

Week 4
- Slight step-up in intensity: aim for one top set per main lift at RPE 8–9 (0–1 RIR).
- Keep total weekly volume controlled (no more than ~10–15% jump from week 1).
- Monitor energy and hunger; if client reports low energy, hold weights equal rather than increase.

Block B — Build (Weeks 5–8)
Goal: increase load and hypertrophy stimulus while maintaining recovery. Include a planned deload in Week 7 (lower volume/intensity).

Week 5
Session A
- Back squat 4×5 (increase load ~5% from baseline)
- Romanian deadlift 3×6
- Bench press 4×6
- Bent-over row 4×6–8
- Side plank 3×30–45s

Session B
- Deadlift 3×4 (heavier: RPE 8 on last set)
- Overhead press 4×6
- Lunges 3×10 each
- Chin-ups or assisted 3×6–8
- Single-leg RDL 3×8 each

Session C
- Hip thrust 4×6–8 (heavier)
- Incline dumbbell press 3×8
- Cable row 3×10
- Leg curl 3×12
- Core circuit (dead bug, bird dog) 3 rounds

Optional conditioning
- Low-intensity interval: 6×1 min easy-hard alternation on bike (1:1 work/rest) overall 12–18 min plus warm-up/cool-down. Keep HR moderate; if stressed, skip.

Nutrition & recovery weeks 5–6
- Maintain protein target.
- If weight loss is goal, keep modest deficit; increase carbohydrate on heavy training days (pre/post).
- Consider distributing total carbs to training days — e.g., a larger breakfast and a pre-workout snack if training in morning.
- Add one focused recovery session weekly: 20–30 min mobility + diaphragmatic breathing.

Week 6
- Continue progressive overload: increase one main lift set weight 2.5–5% or add a rep.
- Keep accessory volume stable.
- Monitor fatigue — if sleep or mood declines, drop accessory sets by 20%.

Week 7 (deload)
- Reduce volume by ~40–50% and intensity by ~10–20%. Keep movement patterns but lighter loads and fewer sets.
- Example: main lifts 2–3 sets of 4–6 at ~60% 1RM; accessories 2×8.
- Emphasize mobility, sleep, and nutrition; reassess readiness for increased stimulus next week.

Week 8
- Resume progression: pick up where left off, aim for heavier singles/doubles on compound lifts for strength focus (3×3–5) and maintain hypertrophy accessory sets.
- Introduce one weekly higher-rep finisher (e.g., 3 rounds of 12–15 banded squat + row) if energy allows.

Block C — Consolidate & Peak (Weeks 9–12)
Goal: consolidate strength/hypertrophy gains, maintain insulin-sensitizing adaptations, prepare for ongoing program post-week 12. Week 12 will be a taper and testing/review.

Week 9
Session A
- Squat 5×5 (moderate-heavy)
- Romanian deadlift 3×6
- Bench press 5×5
- Weighted or heavy-assisted pull-up/chin 4×6
- Farmer carry 3×40m

Session B
- Deadlift 4×4 (heavier)
- Overhead press 4×6
- Reverse lunge 3×8 each
- Dumbbell row 4×8
- Core: hanging knee raise 3×10

Session C
- Hip thrust 4×6
- Incline DB press 3×8
- Single-leg RDL 3×10
- Machine leg curl 3×12
- Glute/ham superset 3 rounds

Week 10
- Slightly increase intensity on priority lifts (aim RPE 8–9 on last sets).
- Keep accessory volume steady. Include one longer tempo set for hypertrophy (e.g., 3×10 slow eccentrics).

Week 11
- Maintain heavy lifts, prioritize technique. If recovery good, add small load increases; if not, keep loads steady and focus on quality.
- Keep conditioning low-volume.

Week 12 (taper & testing)
- Reduce volume ~30–40% and test primary lifts for 3-rep or 5-rep max to measure progress (optional). Alternatively, use RPE-based subjective assessment if testing causes stress.
- Review body composition markers, HbA1c strategy, sleep, subjective energy.
- Plan next 12-week cycle based on progress.

Example session templates (to rotate)
- Strength focus (45–60 min): 10 min warm-up, main lift 4–5 sets, secondary lift 3–4 sets, 2 accessory supersets, core, cool-down.
- Hypertrophy focus (60–75 min): 8–10 sets compound at moderate load, 6–8 accessory sets for targeted muscle groups, metabolic finisher (optional 4–8 min), mobility cool-down.

Conditioning guidance (low-stress)
- 1×/week optional short METCON: 12–18 min bike or row alternating 1–2 min harder, 1–2 min easy. Keep perceived difficulty moderate.
- Walking after meals (10–20 min) is a low-stress strategy to improve glycemic response and insulin sensitivity—encourage daily light movement.

Nutrition specifics (practical)
- Protein: 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day split across 3–4 meals; include 20–40 g high-quality protein per meal.
- Carbs: prioritize around training (pre 30–90 min, post 0–90 min). Aim for moderate intake (e.g., 2–4 g/kg depending on total calories and activity) — if weight loss is desired, err to lower end but keep enough to fuel sessions.
- Fat: 20–30% of calories to support hormones (include omega-3s).
- Avoid prolonged fasting >12–14 hours regularly while in deficit since under-fuelling may worsen HPA dysfunction.
- Emphasize low-GI carbs and fiber, vegetables, legumes, and regular protein-rich snacks.
- Hydration: 2–3 L/day baseline, more around sessions as needed.
- Consider discussing metformin or other pharmacologic therapies with endocrinologist (if not already), as exercise + meds can be additive for insulin sensitivity.

Supplement suggestions (optional; check with her physician)
- Vitamin D if low; omega-3 if intake low; a multivitamin if diet limited.
- Creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day can help strength and body composition and is generally safe — discuss with medical team.

Monitoring & red flags
- Track sleep, mood, menstrual changes, energy, and resting heart rate. If persistent fatigue, mood disruption, appetite suppression, or declining performance occur, reduce volume and consult with medical team.
- Avoid adding long high-intensity cardio sessions in response to plateaus. Instead, adjust diet modestly and maintain strength work.
- Encourage regular follow-ups (every 2–4 weeks) to adjust training loads and nutrition based on progress and labs (HbA1c recheck timeline should be decided with her endocrinologist — changes may take 2–3 months to show).

Sample 4-week microcycle to follow any block (easy-to-copy)
Week (example heavy week)
- Mon: Squat 4×5, Bench 4×6, Bent-over row 3×8, Core 3 sets
- Wed: Deadlift 3×4, Overhead press 4×6, Bulgarian split squats 3×8 each, Pull-downs 3×10
- Fri: Hip thrust 4×8, Incline DB press 3×10, Single-arm row 3×10 each, Hamstring curl 3×12
- Sat/Sun: 20–30 min walk or mobility session; optional conditioning every 7–10 days

Final notes and next steps
- Start 2026-06-01 with Block A Week 1 as outlined.
- Use RPE/RIR and subjective readiness to auto-regulate loading—this is essential given PCOS, irregular cycles, and HPA sensitivity.
- Encourage food logging for 1–2 weeks early on to ensure adequate protein/calories, then shift to a maintenance tracking approach rather than rigid dieting.
- Offer to produce an individualized daily meal plan, grocery list, or a spreadsheet of progressive loads (%) if you want more detailed loading prescriptions (e.g., estimated 1RM percentages) or specific exercise substitution options for any gym equipment limitations.

If you want, tell me:
- Estimated bodyweight (kg) so I can give exact protein/energy targets and %1RM load tables.
- If she prefers morning or evening training, and whether she has any exercise restrictions or previous injuries.
- Whether you want a printable 12-week calendar with loads and progression percentages.
